issues: Brief §8 makes GP1's physical 64/64 pass a hard gate — "nothing downstream is printed until GP1 passes" — but BUILD_NOTES.md states plainly "No printer ran, no slicer ran." All 14 production parts (plug_01, shell_01, pin_r1-r8, key_01, etc.) were nonetheless fully modeled and marked built/validated by geometric checks alone. The mechanism's own arithmetic (brief §5, C5) admits a worst-case engagement of only 0.30 mm on the one dimension the entire game depends on, and that number has zero physical confirmation.

Brief §7 flags the shell at 21 h, over the 20 h gate, and prescribes an open-frame redesign to reach ~19.5 h. DEVIATIONS.md C1 confirms the redesign was made, but adds "Print time was not measured — no slicer ran — so no hour claim is made." The $47-52 COGS estimate and the 20 h gate are therefore both unresolved for the shipped geometry.

None of the five named 'Approved look' pass criteria (free 0-90° turn; protractor marks at 4/20/36/52/68/90°±1°; shoulder flat r=34.6±0.15; slug nose at 22.4±0.15; hood no-sight-line at 400 mm) appear by name among the checks BUILD_NOTES.md lists as having run (layout, build, check_fit, check_mesh, interfere, motion). The hood no-sight-line check is the exact axis this rubric singles out as FAIL-grade (the Armillary precedent) and it is not confirmed anywhere in the artifacts.

Every 'assembled' render (assembled.png, assembled_lane.png, assembled_top.png) shows hood_01 floating disconnected beside the lock rather than seated over it. No render demonstrates the hood actually closing over the chimneys, so the kit's central hidden-state promise (brief §6, the reason the mechanism is print-load-bearing at all) is unverified by anything a reviewer can look at.
